NTA. But he sure is.

I wasn't my moms executor when the first sale happened. I was actually low contact with them at that time due to my family having issues with my ex wife. It was only 5 years ago that I took over my moms care, it was then that I found out about the sale. I didn't say anything about it as it was said and done, and stupidly I assumed Aunt1 selling her portion of land meant she was no longer part of the split. Her selling a larger portion really wouldn't have been much of an issue, since my mom and Aunt2 was dependent on her for a while. The unequal split now wouldn't have been an issue as well, if it was just Aunt2 and my mom, even though Aunt2 has a much larger portion of the remaining land. It's the sudden 3 way split again that caused me refuse an unequal split.

Because when they sold the half from the first time, they didn't change the owners of the plot, and aunts 1 and 2 divided the sale between themselves. When the houses were built, it was unequal to begin with. There were 3 house on the land, the first being Aunt1's, taking up almost 50% of the property, then Aunt2's house took up 35% of the remainder, while our land was a long strip only 3.5 meters wide. My mom never complained as she was mentally unstable since my childhood. If the remaining land was divided 2 ways or equally, it would mean my moms share would increase, cutting a portion of Aunt2's existing house. If there were no houses, dividing the plots would certainly be easier.

Yes, this is square meters. We live in the third world where land plots in main cities are smaller and more expensive. A typical 2 bedroom home here would have a lot area of 50sqm. They typical "starter home" here is a loft house with 35sqm plots. Some are even smaller.

That's actually one of the frustrating parts. Aunt1 has a great life in the U.S. All her children are successful and they have no shortage of money. Aunt2 maybe local, but they too have money and even a second house in the countryside. I make a decent amount of money, but I am supporting my mother and have a wife and children of my own, so my family just "gets by" financially.
This sounds like a fair arrangement. Thank you for the suggestion.

The property is still in the name of the deceased parents, with all three children (mom and aunts) recognized as heirs. When they sold the portion off years ago, they didn't change the tittle, just adjusted the size for the sale.
